bull.b: Raised guidance despite excluding PAD, ENHANCE Part B and DENOVO revenue indicates strong underlying OCS adoption. Continued product, service and logistics growth provides a durable base for expanding transplant volumes and recurring consumables revenue.

Growth in services and logistics broadens TransMedics beyond equipment sales and strengthens its integrated transplant workflow. These activities can increase customer dependence, support recurring case-based revenue and improve the platform’s competitive position.

bull.t: Strong Liquidity and Positive Cash Generation
bull.b: A substantial cash position and positive operating cash flow give TransMedics capacity to fund clinical development, logistics expansion and product investment internally. This supports long-term growth while reducing immediate reliance on external capital.

bear.b: Accelerated spending on OCS Kidney, Gen 3.0, ENHANCE and DENOVO is reducing near-term operating leverage. Although these programs may expand the addressable market, sustained investment could delay margin recovery and increase execution requirements.

bear.t: Rising Leverage and Weaker Free-Cash-Flow Conversion
bear.b: Higher leverage reduces financial flexibility if profitability softens, while weaker free-cash-flow conversion indicates that growth is absorbing more capital through investment or working capital. This raises sensitivity to delays in volume expansion and margin improvement.

Future growth depends partly on regulatory approvals, reimbursement progress and successful PAD integration. Delays could postpone new organ indications and international scale, while near-term dilution from PAD may pressure margins before strategic benefits emerge.
